title: Spike: which devices an operator's own server can notify without a project-run service
description: Serves "Nothing about a film or a viewer … is sent outside the operator's servers, with one exception a viewer chooses"; goal 5, "Postgres is the only required service". The spike comes before JS-212's Spec (D-20261127-notifications-verify-first): no commitment and no PRODUCT.md change until it reports.
acceptanceCriteria: For each platform (iOS through APNs; Android phone and TV through FCM; Android through UnifiedPush; Octave Web through Web Push in Chrome, Firefox and Safari), it is recorded, with an app built and signed by a party other than the server's operator, whether the operator's server delivers a notification using only credentials it holds. Each record names what the operator must obtain, which outside service the message passes through, and what that service sees.
Where a platform needs the publisher's credentials or a relay, the spike says so and names the options (a relay, credentials, no notifications on that platform). It recommends none.
Recorded in docs/ with the versions and commands. The result goes to the product owner before JS-212's Spec.
notes: Ask of Octave, relayed by the owner: "Which push paths will your apps accept: UnifiedPush on Android, Web Push in Octave Web, APNs only on iOS? And would your published apps ever let an operator's server send to them without a relay you run?"
